{{Short description|2026 software security vulnerability}} {{Current||current cybersecurity incident|date=October 2026}} {{Infobox bug | name = PHP2Shell | CVE = {{CVE|2026-109618}}
{{CVE|2026-109619}} | image = File:Wikimedia Phabricator PHP2Shell.png | caption = Wikimedia's [[Phabricator]] instance as seen hours before the patch, having been disabled as a precaution | discovered = | patched = {{Start date and age|df=yes|2026|10|21}} | discoverer = {{Plain list| * [[Wiz, Inc.|Wiz]] * [[OpenAI]] * Calif }} | affected software = [[PHP]] versions 5.4{{endash}}8.5{{cite web |title=PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet {{!}} Wiz Blog |url=https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-php-rce |website=wiz.io |ref=Wiz |language=en-us |date=21 October 2026}} }} '''CVE-2026-109618''' and '''CVE-2026-109619''', collectively referred to as '''PHP2Shell''', are two [[Vulnerability (computer security)|vulnerabilities]] in [[PHP]] versions 5.4 –8.5 that allow [[Arbitrary code execution|remote code execution]]. Their existence was publicly announced on 20 October 2026.{{Cite web |date=2026-10-20 |title=PHP: News Archive - 20 Oct 2026 |url=https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-20-1 |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=www.php.net |language=en}} An emergency patch and details about the vulnerabilities were released on the following day.{{Cite web |date=2026-10-21 |title=PHP: News Archive - 21 Oct 2026 |url=https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php#2026-10-21-5|access-date=2026-10-21 |website=www.php.net |language=en}} ==Discovery== The vulnerabilities were independently discovered by the California-based security firm Calif as part of the [[OpenAI]] "Patch the Planet" project in August 2026, and by the Israeli-American cloud security company [[Wiz (company)|Wiz, Inc]].{{cite press release|title=Patch the Planet: global response coordination as agents uncover critical vulnerabilities |url=https://openai.com/index/coordinated-disclosure-of-critical-vulnerabilities/ |website=OpenAI |access-date=21 October 2026 |date=21 October 2026}}{{Self-published inline |date=October 2026}}{{cite news |last1=McMillan |first1=Robert |title=Exclusive {{!}} AI Just Found a Bug That Puts up to 70% of the World’s Websites at Risk |url=https://www.wsj.com/tech/cybersecurity/ai-just-found-a-bug-that-puts-up-to-70-of-the-worlds-websites-at-risk-fd0902ea |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=Wall Street Journal |date=21 October 2026}} PHP versions as early as 5.4 are affected, and while the security flaw had been identified decades earlier, it was not fixed at the time as it was not thought that an exploit would be feasible.{{cite news |last1=Khandelwal |first1=Swati |title=PHP Issues Emergency Patches for Two Critical PHP2Shell RCE Flaws as Exploit Attempts Emerge |url=https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/php-issues-emergency-patches-for-two.html |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=The Hacker News |date=21 October 2026 |language=en}} The vulnerability was rated 9.2 (critical) out of 10 under [[Common Vulnerability Scoring System|CVSS]] v4.0 by PHP developers,{{Cite web |title=php.announce: [ANNOUNCE] Upcoming Critical PHP Security Release |url=https://news-web.php.net/php.announce/509 |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=news-web.php.net}} while security firm watchTowr rated it a full 10.0.{{Cite web |last=Abrams |first=Lawrence |title=PHP warns admins of two critical flaws, emergency patches coming tomorrow |url=https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/php-warns-admins-of-two-critical-flaws-emergency-patches-coming-tomorrow/ |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=BleepingComputer |language=en-us}} ==Patches== The maintainers of PHP released patched versions of PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5. Source code patches were released for version 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, but no official updated binaries for those versions were released as they are considered [[Software release life cycle#End-of-life|end of life]]. Both vulnerabilities were published through GitHub security advisories{{cite web|url=https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w|title=RCE via OOM corruption|date=2026-10-21|access-date=2026-10-21}}{{cite web|url=https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp|title=RCE via stale global state|date=2026-10-21|access-date=2026-10-21}} on 21 October at 13:34 UTC, 26 minutes before the announced release time, with the PHP website updated shortly thereafter. The PHP maintainers announced the update early and before release, after news of the vulnerabilities leaked on the [[Hacker News]] forums and was confirmed by the [[X (social network)|X]] account of cybersecurity company watchTowr labs.{{cite news |last1=Khandelwal |first1=Swati |title=PHP2Shell: Two Unpatched Critical PHP RCE Flaws (CVSS 9.2) Trigger Emergency Security Alert |url=https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/php2shell-two-unpatched-critical-php.html |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=The Hacker News |date=21 October 2026 |language=en}} The early notice on PHP.net encouraged users to prepare and update as soon as the patch was released. One security firm, Sansec, expected "mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release".{{Cite web |last=Goodin |first=Dan |date=2026-10-21 |title=PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently |url=https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10/php-maintainers-tell-web-devs-to-prepare-themselves-for-critical-security-patches/ |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=Ars Technica |language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261021121524/https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10/php-maintainers-tell-web-devs-to-prepare-themselves-for-critical-security-patches/|archive-date=2026-10-21|url-status=live}} [[Proof of concept|PoCs]], write-ups, and partial mitigations started circulating on the Internet before the end of the embargo.{{Cite web |title=Only for the curious... |url=https://jackalsyn.com/posts/php-up-2026.html |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=jackalsyn.com}} [[Cloudflare]] reported signs of early exploitation prior to public [[Patch (computing)|patch]] release, and deployed temporary [[web application firewall]] (WAF) rules as an attempted stopgap mitigation against the [[Vulnerability (computer security)|vulnerability]].{{cite web |last1=Knecht |first1=Dane |title=Dane Knecht 🦭 (@dok2001) on X |url=https://x.com/dok2001/status/2112811965735202970 |website=X (formerly Twitter) |date=21 October 2026}}{{Cite news |date=2026-10-21 |title=Hold on to your butts: Web admins braced for emergency PHP updates to plug leaked exploits |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/software/security/we-expect-mass-attacks-to-start-within-15-minutes-of-the-release-web-admins-braced-for-emergency-php-updates-to-plug-leaked-high-severity-holes/ |access-date=2026-10-21 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}} == Impact == Approximately 69% of websites use PHP, including those that use [[content management system]]s such as [[Drupal]], [[Joomla]], and [[WordPress]], so the potential impacts were widespread.{{cite news |last1=Collier |first1=Kevin |title=Critical vulnerabilities in commonly used web code spark rush to update systems |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/security/critical-vulnerabilities-php-update-systems-rcna604751 |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=NBC News |date=21 October 2026 |language=en}}{{cite news |last1=Gerkin |first1=Tom |title=Websites taken down worldwide as critical PHP cyber-security update issued |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmly0lg3w5x2o |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=BBC News |date=21 October 2026}} Following advice from [[Computer emergency response team|CERT]]-EU and the British [[National Cyber Security Centre (United Kingdom)|National Cyber Security Centre]], many organizations across Europe took their websites offline as a precaution while the patches were pending, including the [[Netherlands|Dutch]] government portal Overheid.nl, the [[Denmark|Danish]] national school communication platform, all [[Finland|Finnish]] government public-facing web services, and [[France|French]] local government administration websites.{{Cite news |last=Satter |first=Raphael |last2=Pardesi |first2=Rajveer |last3=Marchandon |first3=Leo |last4=Satter |first4=Raphael |last5=Marchandon |first5=Leo |date=2026-10-21 |title=Government websites go dark as software flaw sparks security scramble |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/eu-agency-warns-websites-may-need-be-taken-offline-php-prepares-patches-2026-10-21/ |access-date=2026-10-21 |work=Reuters |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2026-10-21 |title=Websites taken down as critical PHP cyber-security update issued |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmly0lg3w5x2o |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Major websites go offline as critical PHP vulnerability triggers security fears |url=https://www.brusselstimes.com/belgium/2371464/major-websites-go-offline-as-critical-php-vulnerability-triggers-security-fears |access-date=2026-10-21 |website=The Brussels Times |language=en}}{{cite press release|url=https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/news/critical-security-issue-affecting-php|publisher=National Cyber Security Centre|date=October 20, 2026|title=Critical security issue affecting PHP}} The US [[National Security Agency]] recommended that websites go offline if unable to update immediately.{{cite news |last1=Kan |first1=Michael |title=This Flaw Is So Serious Websites Should Consider Going Offline, NSA Says |url=https://www.pcmag.com/news/php-flaw-is-so-serious-websites-should-consider-going-offline-nsa-says |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=PCMAG |date=21 October 2026 |language=en}} The [[Wikimedia Foundation]] shut down many of their supporting services, and forum sites [[4Chan|4chan]] and [[Something Awful]] went offline.{{cite news |title=Impact of PHP vulnerabilities on Wikimedia tools and services |url=https://diff.wikimedia.org/2026/10/21/impact-of-php-vulnerabilities-on-wikimedia-tools-and-services/ |access-date=21 October 2026 |work=Diff |publisher=Wikimedia Foundation |date=21 October 2026}} Parts of the [[Japan]]ese internet also went offline, including games such as ''[[Umamusume: Pretty Derby]]'' and ''[[Shadowverse: Worlds Beyond]]'', and many online commerce sites.{{cite news|url=https://www.itmedia.co.jp/news/article/2610/21/2000002472/|date=October 21, 2026|title=著名ITサービス相次いで緊急メンテへ　コドモン、シャドバ、BASE、さくらのレンタルサーバなど　「PHP」脆弱性に起因か|publisher=ITmedia}} == See also == * [[Log4Shell]] * [[Heartbleed]] == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == *
